name: Warm Up — Deep Breathing
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides.
Inhale slowly through your nose for 4 counts, letting your belly rise.
Hold for 2 counts, then exhale through your mouth for 6 counts.
Repeat 5–6 cycles, gradually deepening each breath.
Feel your body awaken and your mind become present.
benefit: Oxygenates the body and centers the mind before practice

name: Warm Up — Neck Rolls
steps: Sit or stand with your spine tall and shoulders relaxed.
Slowly drop your right ear toward your right shoulder. Hold 5 seconds.
Roll your chin down to your chest, then left ear to left shoulder.
Complete 3 slow full rotations in each direction.
Never roll the head backward — keep movements gentle and controlled.
benefit: Releases tension in the neck and upper trapezius

name: Warm Up — Shoulder Circles
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, arms loose at your sides.
Lift both shoulders up toward your ears, then roll them back and down.
Make large, slow circles — 10 rotations backward, then 10 forward.
Focus on maximum range of motion, especially rolling them back.
Feel the chest open and the shoulder blades draw together.
benefit: Loosens the shoulder joint and opens the chest

name: Warm Up — Waist Rotations
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hands on hips.
Keep your hips stable as you rotate your upper body to the right.
Come back to center, then rotate to the left. This is one rep.
Gradually increase the range of motion with each rotation.
Complete 15 rotations on each side, breathing freely.
benefit: Warms up the lumbar spine and obliques

name: Warm Up — Jogging in Place
steps: Begin jogging in place at a comfortable, relaxed pace.
Land softly on the balls of your feet to protect your knees.
Swing your arms naturally to build momentum and raise your heart rate.
After 2 minutes, increase pace slightly for the last 3 minutes.
Focus on steady breathing — inhale through the nose, exhale through the mouth.
benefit: Elevates heart rate and warms all muscle groups

name: Surya Namaskar
steps: Begin in Pranamasana (prayer pose) — stand at the mat's edge, feet together, palms at chest.
Inhale: raise arms overhead into Hastauttanasana, gently arching the back.
Exhale: fold forward into Hastapadasana, touching the floor beside your feet.
Inhale: step the right foot back into a low lunge (Ashwa Sanchalanasana).
Exhale: step the left foot back into Phalakasana (plank). Breathe steadily.
Lower knees, chest, and chin to the mat — Ashtanga Namaskara.
Inhale: glide forward into Bhujangasana (cobra), lifting the chest.
Exhale: lift hips high into Adho Mukha Svanasana (downward dog). Hold 5 breaths.
Inhale: step the right foot forward into a lunge. Exhale: bring the left foot to meet it.
Inhale: rise slowly, sweeping arms overhead. Exhale: return to Pranamasana.
benefit: Full-body awakening — stretches, strengthens, and energizes every system

name: Matsyasan
steps: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and arms alongside your body.
Slide your hands under your hips, palms facing down.
Press your elbows into the floor and inhale to lift your chest off the mat.
Tilt your head back and gently rest the crown of the head on the mat.
Keep most of the weight on your elbows — avoid straining the neck.
Breathe deeply into the chest, feeling it open and expand.
Hold the pose steadily for the duration, then gently release by lifting the head first.
benefit: Opens the chest and throat, counteracts forward-hunching postures

name: Ardha Matsyendriyasan
steps: Sit with both legs extended in front of you (Dandasana).
Bend your right knee and place the right foot flat on the floor outside the left thigh.
Bend your left knee and tuck the left foot near your right hip.
Inhale and sit tall, lengthening your spine upward.
Exhale and twist to the right, wrapping your left arm around your right knee.
Place your right hand on the floor behind your right hip for support.
With each inhale, grow taller; with each exhale, deepen the twist gently.
Hold, then release and repeat on the opposite side.
benefit: Massages abdominal organs, improves spinal mobility and digestion

name: Ushthrasan
steps: Kneel on your mat with knees hip-width apart and thighs perpendicular to the floor.
Place your hands on your lower back, fingers pointing downward, for initial support.
Inhale and lift through your chest, drawing the shoulder blades together.
Slowly lean back, reaching one hand at a time toward your heels.
Let your head fall back gently — only if there is no neck strain.
Push your hips forward to keep them above the knees; avoid collapsing.
Breathe deeply into your chest. To release, bring hands to hips and rise on an inhale.
benefit: Deep chest and hip flexor opener, energizes the spine

name: Supta Vajrasan
steps: Begin in Vajrasana — sit on your heels with the spine straight.
Place your hands behind you, fingers pointing forward, and lean back onto your elbows.
Continue lowering until the crown of your head or the back of your head rests on the mat.
Cross your arms over your chest or extend them overhead on the floor.
Keep the knees on the mat — if they lift, place a folded blanket under them.
Relax your facial muscles and breathe slowly and deeply.
To come out, use your elbows to gradually lift yourself back to Vajrasana.
benefit: Stretches quadriceps and hip flexors; improves digestion

name: Uttana Padasan
steps: Lie on your back with legs extended and arms flat alongside your body.
Press your lower back firmly into the mat and engage your core.
Inhale and slowly raise both legs together to a 45-degree angle.
Point your toes forward and keep your legs straight and together.
Hold the position without letting the legs drop, breathing steadily.
If needed, you may also raise your head and shoulders slightly off the mat.
Slowly lower the legs on an exhale. Rest, then repeat 3–4 times.
benefit: Strengthens the core and lower abdominal muscles

name: Naukasan
steps: Lie flat on your back with legs together and arms at your sides.
Inhale deeply. On the exhale, simultaneously lift your head, shoulders, arms, and legs off the mat.
Balance on your tailbone — your body should form a V shape.
Extend your arms forward, parallel to the floor, fingers pointing toward your feet.
Hold the gaze forward or slightly upward. Keep breathing — do not hold your breath.
Maintain the position as long as comfortable, then slowly lower back down.
Relax in Shavasana for a few breaths before repeating.
benefit: Tones the entire core, improves balance and concentration

name: Sarvangasan
steps: Lie on your back. Bend your knees and draw them toward your chest.
Use your hands to support your lower back as you lift your hips off the floor.
Straighten your legs upward toward the ceiling, forming a straight line.
Your weight should rest on the back of your shoulders and upper arms — not on your neck.
Keep your elbows close together and support your back with both hands.
Gaze up at your toes and breathe slowly. Avoid turning your head.
To release, bend your knees to your chest and roll down one vertebra at a time.
benefit: Stimulates the thyroid, improves circulation and calms the nervous system

name: Halasan
steps: From Sarvangasan, begin to lower your legs overhead behind you.
Let your toes touch the floor behind your head, if comfortable.
Keep supporting your back with your hands, or extend your arms flat on the mat.
If your toes don't reach the floor, maintain them where they are without forcing.
Keep the legs straight and active. Breathe long and slow.
Hold the position, then slowly roll down vertebra by vertebra with control.
Rest in Shavasana to allow the spine to decompress.
benefit: Deep spinal stretch, calms the nervous system and improves flexibility

name: Marjalasan
steps: Begin on all fours — wrists under shoulders, knees under hips (Table Top).
Inhale: drop your belly toward the floor, lift your chest and tailbone (Cow).
Exhale: round your spine toward the ceiling, tuck chin to chest (Cat).
Move fluidly between Cat and Cow, one full breath per movement.
Keep the movement slow and deliberate — let the breath lead the motion.
Feel each vertebra articulate as you wave through the spine.
Complete 10 full Cat-Cow cycles, then rest in Child's Pose.
benefit: Mobilizes the entire spine, relieves back tension

name: Dhanurasana
steps: Lie on your stomach with your chin resting on the mat, arms at your sides.
Bend both knees and bring your heels toward your buttocks.
Reach back with both hands and firmly grasp your ankles (not toes).
Inhale and simultaneously lift your chest and thighs off the mat.
Your body should form the shape of a bow — head up, legs pulling upward.
Keep pressing the ankles back into your hands to deepen the arch.
Rock gently with the breath if desired. Release slowly on an exhale.
benefit: Full back-body stretch, opens the chest and hip flexors

name: Natarajasan
steps: Stand tall in Tadasana. Shift your weight onto your left foot.
Bend your right knee and bring the right heel toward your right buttock.
Reach back with your right hand and hold the inside of your right ankle or foot.
Inhale and raise your left arm forward and upward, parallel to the floor.
Kick your right foot back and up, lifting the leg while leaning slightly forward.
Your body will tilt into a graceful arch — find a focal point (drishti) to balance.
Hold, then release with control. Repeat on the left side.
benefit: Improves balance, stretches the chest, shoulders, and hip flexors

name: Janu Shirshasan
steps: Sit in Dandasana with both legs extended. Bend your right knee.
Place the sole of your right foot against your inner left thigh.
Inhale and extend your spine tall, raising your arms overhead.
Exhale and hinge forward from your hips over your extended left leg.
Hold your left foot, ankle, or calf — wherever you can reach without rounding the back.
With each inhale, lengthen the spine; with each exhale, fold a little deeper.
Hold, then switch sides — extend the right leg and bend the left.
benefit: Deep hamstring and lower back stretch, calms the mind

name: Badha Konasan
steps: Sit upright with both legs extended. Bend both knees and bring the soles of your feet together.
Draw your heels as close toward your pelvis as is comfortable.
Hold your feet with both hands, interlacing the fingers around them.
Sit tall and press your knees gently toward the floor — never force them down.
Inhale and lengthen the spine. If comfortable, hinge slightly forward from the hips.
Breathe slowly and allow the inner thighs to gradually release.
Hold, then gently use your hands to lift the knees before extending the legs.
benefit: Opens the hips and groin, stimulates the reproductive and urinary organs

name: Katwangasan
steps: Begin in Dandasana. Bend both knees and bring them toward your chest.
Lean back slightly, balancing on your tailbone with the spine tall.
Extend both arms forward, parallel to the floor, at shoulder height.
Slowly extend the legs upward and forward at a 45–60 degree angle.
Your body forms a V — balance on the sit bones, not the tailbone.
Keep the core engaged and the chest open. Breathe steadily.
Hold, then lower the legs slowly and rest.
benefit: Strengthens the core and hip flexors, improves balance

name: Meru Dandasan
steps: Lie on your back with arms extended at shoulder level forming a T.
Bend your right knee and place the right foot flat on the floor.
Inhale, and on the exhale, slowly drop the right knee across the body to the left.
Turn your head to the right, creating a gentle spinal twist.
Keep both shoulders flat on the floor — do not let the right shoulder lift.
Breathe into the twist, relaxing deeper with each exhale.
Return to center and repeat on the other side.
benefit: Releases the lumbar spine and sacrum, reduces lower back tension

name: Trataka
steps: Sit in a comfortable meditation posture — Sukhasana or Vajrasana.
Place a candle flame at eye level, about 60–90 cm in front of you.
Gaze softly and steadily at the tip of the flame without blinking.
If tears form, that is natural — allow the eyes to release tension.
When you must blink, close the eyes gently and visualize the flame internally.
When the image fades, open the eyes and resume steady gazing.
Continue the practice with complete stillness of body and breath.
benefit: Improves concentration, strengthens eye muscles, calms the mind

name: Setu Bandhasana
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart.
Place your feet close to your buttocks — about a hand's width away.
Arms rest flat beside your body, palms facing down.
Inhale and press your feet and arms into the floor, lifting your hips upward.
Interlace your fingers beneath your lifted hips and press the arms down.
Roll your shoulders underneath you to open the chest further.
Hold, breathing into the chest, then slowly lower vertebra by vertebra on an exhale.
benefit: Strengthens the back and glutes, opens the chest and hip flexors

name: Mandukasan
steps: Begin in Vajrasana. Make fists with both hands, placing the thumbs inside.
Place both fists on your lower abdomen, on either side of your navel.
Inhale deeply. On the exhale, lean forward pressing the fists into the abdomen.
Look forward and hold the position while retaining the exhale (Bahir Kumbhaka).
Hold as long as comfortable, then inhale and return to upright Vajrasana.
Relax for a few breaths before repeating. Complete 3–5 rounds.
Avoid this pose if you have recent abdominal surgery or ulcers.
benefit: Massages the pancreas and abdominal organs, supports diabetes management

name: Anjaneyasana
steps: Start in Downward Dog. Step your right foot forward between your hands.
Lower your left knee to the mat and slide it back until you feel a stretch in the left hip flexor.
Untuck the left toes and press the top of the left foot into the mat.
Inhale and raise both arms alongside your ears, palms facing each other.
Lift through the chest and engage the core to protect the lower back.
Gently draw the tailbone down and the pubic bone forward.
Hold and breathe, then return to Downward Dog and repeat on the left side.
benefit: Deep hip flexor stretch, builds strength and opens the heart

name: Shavasana
steps: Lie flat on your back, allowing your feet to fall open naturally.
Let your arms rest away from your body, palms facing upward.
Close your eyes and release all effort from every muscle in your body.
Begin a body scan: consciously relax your feet, calves, thighs, hips, abdomen...
Continue releasing the chest, shoulders, arms, neck, jaw, and forehead.
Breathe naturally without controlling the breath. Simply observe.
Remain completely still and surrender to stillness for the full duration.
benefit: Integrates the practice, restores the nervous system, deepens relaxation
